properties: Single installation owner; validation precedes replacement; failure preserves runnable installation
assessment: real setup/update/platform process evidence; no runnable-installation proof from abstract model alone
remaining: OS service managers and downloaded artifacts require supported-platform CI/live evidence; environment-gated checks must report prerequisites/skips.
evidenceDecision: Real setup/update/service tests exercise verified assets, replacement failures, request budgets, saved default diagnostic precedence, package/plugin and preview ownership guards, and moved generated service paths without forcing custom definitions. Native plugin compatibility and system installers add checksum, metadata, native-support and failed-promotion checks; a compiled fixture with an isolated home and empty PATH verifies all frozen action verbs and canonical service ownership. Native fixture lifecycle tests cover awaited bounded cleanup, transient/persistent filesystem denial, nonretryable failure and preservation of both body/cleanup errors; this does not identify an earlier native lock holder or imply its body passed. Explicit running setup tests exercise registration without activation, discovery/registration refusal, directory/non-executable preservation before service mutation, and real bootstrap callers through CLI and confirmed HTTP. Mocked systemd/launchd/Task Scheduler command traces establish emitted registration-only sequences, not actual OS login behavior. Windows installer and macOS launchd execution remain platform CI evidence. Proposed installer-upgrade CI builds real native candidate archives and exercises latest-stable plugin installation, authenticated runtime/session migration and failed-checksum retention in isolated state. Herdr installs and upgrades use fake Herdr binaries, installers and servers: checksum and version checks precede replacement, a failed check restores the previous binary, newer and package-managed installs stay untouched, version-manager shims are never replaced, a newer or unidentified running server is never handed to the verified release, and live handoff is requested only for a Linux server proven to run outside any supervisor (a daemonized server in a scope; fake procfs cases include an operator-owned systemd unit and a wrapper parent; macOS is never proven), a v0.2.6 versioned legacy Windows Herdr is found off PATH and migrated, and install.ps1 release directories on PATH are recognized as official; otherwise the old server keeps running and a restart is reported. The installer-upgrade matrix runs the real candidate `herdr upgrade` against a compiled fake Herdr on each native platform to prove harness-integration installation and plugin tag pinning. Installer shell regressions exercise the new-binary finalization handoff, Herdr opt-out and older pinned-release fallback; mocked systemd/launchd traces verify that the shared CLI update finalization reports Herdr/integration/plugin output, restarts the matching active service after Herdr failure and explains skipped or failed restarts without another World download. This direct platform evidence is more useful than a model of OS packaging; OS service/channel upgrades and older release combinations remain excluded (docs/release.md). Mutation regressions execute the CLI shell verifier against valid archives, wrong digests, wrong package and executable versions, and wrong-platform manifests; in-app wrong-VERSION rejection is exercised independently.
